questions.question: Which prompt elements distinguish what the model should do from the information it should use?

options.text: An instruction that states the task.
options.explanation: Instructions specify the operation or goal.

options.text: A temperature value used as the task description.
options.explanation: Temperature changes sampling behavior; it does not describe the task.

options.text: Context that supplies relevant background or reference material.
options.explanation: Context gives information needed to carry out the task.

options.text: A longer response limit used as a replacement for requirements.
options.explanation: An output budget does not explain what the answer must contain.

questions.takeaway: State the task explicitly and supply the context needed to perform it.

questions.question: A prompt mixes employee policy text with instructions in one paragraph. The bot sometimes treats policy text as part of the task. Which revision best clarifies the structure?

options.text: Repeat the entire paragraph several times.
options.explanation: Repetition increases length without distinguishing task and reference material.

options.text: Place reference text inside clear delimiters and state the task separately.
options.explanation: The lesson uses delimiters to distinguish content to process from instructions.

options.text: Remove the policy text and ask the model to recall it.
options.explanation: Removing required private knowledge sacrifices the evidence needed for the answer.

options.text: Increase the maximum output length.
options.explanation: Output length does not repair the prompt’s structural ambiguity.

questions.takeaway: Use clear boundaries between instructions, reference context, and the user’s question.

questions.question: A correct technical answer is too advanced for new employees. Which prompt changes directly address that mismatch?

options.text: Ask for more domain jargon to establish authority.
options.explanation: Additional jargon makes the answer harder for this audience to understand.

options.text: Identify the audience as new employees with no technical background.
options.explanation: Audience information helps the model choose the right depth and vocabulary.

options.text: Remove the factual reference material.
options.explanation: Accuracy still needs the reference material; the mismatch is in presentation.

options.text: Specify an onboarding instructor role and ask for a plain-language explanation.
options.explanation: Role and style instructions guide a more suitable presentation of the same facts.

questions.takeaway: Role and audience guide how information is explained, while reference material grounds its content.

questions.question: A downstream parser expects an object with “answer” and “department” fields, but the bot returns prose. What is the most direct prompt improvement?

options.text: Specify JSON with the required fields and instruct the model to omit surrounding prose.
options.explanation: An explicit output format communicates the parser’s expectations. Validate the result in application code as well.

options.text: Ask for a friendlier tone.
options.explanation: Tone does not define a machine-readable structure.

options.text: Add unrelated examples of long essays.
options.explanation: These examples encourage the wrong output structure.

options.text: Increase top_p to produce more formatting variety.
options.explanation: More variation does not help satisfy a fixed output contract.

questions.takeaway: Specify the required output structure explicitly; a prompt is not a substitute for validation.

questions.question: The bot follows the requested headings but its style varies widely. Which changes follow the lesson’s few-shot approach?

options.text: Add representative examples of the desired input-output behavior.
options.explanation: Examples demonstrate the target style and structure concretely.

options.text: Paste any available examples even if they contradict the required format.
options.explanation: Conflicting examples create mixed signals instead of a useful pattern.

options.text: Keep examples consistent with the explicit instructions.
options.explanation: Consistent examples reinforce rather than compete with the intended behavior.

options.text: Assume the examples permanently update model weights.
options.explanation: Few-shot examples are supplied in the prompt; they do not constitute weight training.

questions.takeaway: Few-shot prompting teaches a pattern through examples in context, without updating model weights.

questions.question: After revising an AI judge prompt, accuracy on development examples rises from 80% to 100%, but evaluation accuracy falls from 82% to 60%. What is the strongest next action?

options.text: Adopt the revision because development accuracy is perfect.
options.explanation: Perfect performance on examples used for revision does not establish generalization.

options.text: Move every failed evaluation example into the development set and report its new score as independent.
options.explanation: That removes the independence of the evaluation and hides the generalization problem.

options.text: Change the labels to match the new judge.
options.explanation: Labels should represent expert standards rather than conform to model mistakes.

options.text: Inspect errors and label consistency, and prefer a prompt supported by evaluation performance.
options.explanation: The lesson uses evaluation degradation to flag overfitting or sample problems and chooses the prompt on evaluation evidence.

questions.takeaway: An AI judge must generalize beyond the examples used to improve its prompt.

questions.question: A team automatically rewrites a Q&A prompt until the model says its answer “looks good.” Which changes make this optimization loop more reliable?

options.text: Compare outputs with representative reference answers.
options.explanation: Reference answers make missing or incorrect content visible during gap analysis.

options.text: Use an explicit evaluation rubric with pass/fail criteria.
options.explanation: A judge with defined criteria gives a more meaningful stopping signal than vague approval.

options.text: Keep optimizing solely against one successful example.
options.explanation: A single example cannot establish general performance and invites overfitting.

options.text: Check performance on evaluation examples not used to rewrite the prompt.
options.explanation: Separate evaluation helps detect a prompt that merely fits the development cases.

questions.takeaway: Prompt optimization needs explicit standards and evidence of generalization.
